 Upstate music teacher sentenced for several child sex crimes 
 FOX Carolina's Anna Arinder has the details. By Mary Kate Howland Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 11:25 AM EDT | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SPARTANBURG, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - The South Carolina Attorney General’s Office confirmed that an Upstate music teacher has been sentenced for several child sex crimes.
 John Foster, Jr., 78, pleaded guilty to third-degree criminal sexual conduct with a minor and two counts of third-degree sexual exploitation of a minor. He was sentenced to 10 years in prison, suspended upon serving 90 days in jail, followed by five years of probation.
 Foster was 75 at the time of the assault. His victim was 13. (Spartanburg Police Department) Officials said that during the week, Foster is on home detention and only allowed to leave his home for medical appointments and church. He is to have no direct or indirect contact with the victim or the family, and he must register as a sex offender and remain on GPS monitoring. 
 Foster was arrested twice in 2024 after police said a teen came forward to report being sexually assaulted by him while taking music lessons at Roper Music on East Main Street in Spartanburg. Police said that while investigating the allegations, they uncovered child pornography .
 The attorney general’s officer shared that while the victim and parents wished for more jail time, they were satisfied that Foster admitted his guilt in court and will be spending time in jail.
